title: QUIC RFC 9000 Application Data Delayed ACK Timer Work Item
summary: Implement and prove the active-path Application Data ACK-delay runtime timer so ordinary ACK-only packets wait for local max_ack_delay while immediate ACK exceptions, packet-count threshold sends, and ACK piggybacking still work.
planned_changes:
- Add a dedicated runtime ACK-delay timer kind and deadline state.
- Arm the timer after ordinary 1-RTT ack-eliciting packet processing when no immediate ACK or packet-count threshold send is required.
- Emit an ACK-only packet at timer expiry without injecting ack-eliciting frames.
- Keep non-ack-eliciting-only receipts from arming the timer.
- Cancel the timer after ACK-only sends or ACK piggybacking on outgoing ack-eliciting packets.
- Preserve Initial, Handshake, path scheduling, interop success, and public API behavior outside this slice.
- Add positive, negative, edge, deterministic fuzz/property, and BenchmarkDotNet coverage for the timer decision path.
verification_plan: Run focused RFC 9000 delayed-ACK requirement-home tests for S13P2P1-0001, S13P2P1-0004, S13P2P1-0012, S13P2P2-0001, and S13P2P2-0002; run the focused ACK piggyback/feedback-loop tests; run the ACK piggyback policy benchmark suite with BenchmarkDotNet Dry and Short jobs; render/check the touched SpecTrace artifacts; run canonical SpecTrace JSON validation and preserve standing failures if present; run `git diff --check`; and preserve evidence under `artifacts/v/20260425-rfc9000-application-ack-delay-timer/` and `artifacts/bb/20260425-rfc9000-application-ack-delay-timer/`.
out_of_scope: ACK frame parser or serializer behavior.
completion_notes: Completed as a bounded active-path Application Data ACK-delay runtime timer floor. The 2026-05-08 topoff added direct S13P2-0002 proof that an ack-eliciting Application Data packet schedules and emits ACK-only output at the advertised max_ack_delay. The later 2026-05-08 S13P2P2-0003 topoff added negative and edge proof for processing multiple packets before deciding whether to send an ACK. Path scheduling and endpoint interop coverage remain separate.
